accepted.s: Which one of the following committees is concerned with sanctions against Al-Qaida, ISIL (Da'esh) and their associates, including terrorist listings?
accepted.x: The 1267 Committee deals with sanctions against Al-Qaida, ISIL (Da'esh) and associated individuals and entities, including terrorist listings.
accepted.tq: Use the subject-based distinction among closely numbered UNSC committees.
accepted.sec: UNSC sanctions and counter-terrorism committees - 1267, 1373, 1540

accepted.s: The Counter-Terrorism Committee was established under which of the following resolutions?
accepted.x: Resolution 1373 of 2001 established the Counter-Terrorism Committee after the 9/11 attacks.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar resolution numbers by linking each number with its subject and year.
accepted.sec: UNSC sanctions and counter-terrorism committees - 1267, 1373, 1540

accepted.s: Resolution 1540 of the United Nations Security Council primarily seeks to prevent
o: the use of veto by permanent members
accepted.x: Resolution 1540 concerns stopping weapons of mass destruction from reaching non-state actors.
accepted.tq: Identify the mandate rather than the resolution number alone.
accepted.sec: UNSC sanctions and counter-terrorism committees - 1267, 1373, 1540

accepted.s: Masood Azhar, associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed, was listed under which United Nations mechanism in 2019?
accepted.x: Masood Azhar was listed under the 1267 Committee in 2019.
accepted.tq: Match the person with the correct committee instead of relying on the organisation alone.
accepted.sec: UNSC sanctions and counter-terrorism committees - 1267, 1373, 1540

accepted.s: India conducted its first capacity-building programme on UNSCR 1540 for Asia-Pacific countries in February 2025 at
accepted.x: The programme was held at the National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN), Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh, in February 2025.
accepted.tq: Test the location and date together; location swaps are common traps.
accepted.sec: UNSC sanctions and counter-terrorism committees - 1267, 1373, 1540

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding groups proposing reform of the United Nations Security Council:
1. The G4 comprises Brazil, Germany, India and Japan.
2. The Uniting for Consensus group is led by Italy and opposes the creation of new permanent seats.
3. China is a member of the G4.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. China is not a member of the G4, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped membership statement in a group-composition question.
accepted.sec: UNSC reform - G4, Uniting for Consensus, L.69, Ezulwini, IGN

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: G4 — Opposition to permanent seats for Africa
Uniting for Consensus — Demand for new permanent seats
L.69 — Developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific
Ezulwini Consensus — Abolition of all non-permanent seats
accepted.x: The L.69 group consists of developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific. The G4 supports permanent seats, Uniting for Consensus opposes new permanent seats, and Ezulwini seeks African representation.
accepted.tq: Use the demand and membership columns to eliminate reversed descriptions.
accepted.sec: UNSC reform - G4, Uniting for Consensus, L.69, Ezulwini, IGN

accepted.s: The Ezulwini Consensus of 2005 demanded for Africa
o: five permanent seats without veto power and two non-permanent seats
two non-permanent seats and five permanent seats
two permanent seats with veto power and five non-permanent seats
one permanent seat without veto power and four non-permanent seats
accepted.x: The African Union's Ezulwini Consensus demands two permanent seats with veto power and five non-permanent seats for Africa.
accepted.tq: Separate the number of permanent seats from the number of non-permanent seats.
accepted.sec: UNSC reform - G4, Uniting for Consensus, L.69, Ezulwini, IGN

accepted.s:
With reference to Inter-Governmental Negotiations (IGN), consider the following statements:
1. It is an informal United Nations General Assembly working group.
2. It was set up in 2008.
3. Its annual Elements Paper maps agreements and disagreements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the IGN and its annual Elements Paper.
accepted.tq: When all statements describe distinct parts of one institutional profile, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: UNSC reform - G4, Uniting for Consensus, L.69, Ezulwini, IGN

accepted.s: A Charter amendment relating to reform of the United Nations Security Council requires approval by
o: two-thirds of the members, including all five permanent members
two-thirds of the permanent members alone
all members of the General Assembly without participation of the P5
a simple majority of all members including any three P5 members
accepted.x: A Charter amendment requires a two-thirds majority of members and ratification by all five permanent members of the Security Council.
accepted.tq: Ask which voting threshold and membership condition apply to the constitutional procedure.
accepted.sec: UNSC reform - G4, Uniting for Consensus, L.69, Ezulwini, IGN

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Secretaries-General of the United Nations in chronological order of assuming office:
A. U Thant
B. Trygve Lie
C. Kurt Waldheim
D. Dag Hammarskjold
accepted.x: The order is Trygve Lie, Dag Hammarskjold, U Thant and Kurt Waldheim, corresponding to 1946, 1953, 1961 and 1972 respectively.
accepted.tq: Fix the first Secretary-General and then place the remaining officeholders by their starting years.
accepted.sec: Secretaries-General - order, FIRST by region, present SG

accepted.s: Who was the first Asian to serve as Secretary-General of the United Nations?
accepted.x: U Thant of Burma, who served from 1961 to 1971, was the first Asian Secretary-General.
accepted.tq: Distinguish regional-first claims from the nationality of later officeholders.
accepted.sec: Secretaries-General - order, FIRST by region, present SG

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Javier Perez de Cuellar — First Latin American Secretary-General — Peru
Boutros Boutros-Ghali — First Latin American Secretary-General — Egypt
Kofi Annan — First Asian Secretary-General — Ghana
Ban Ki-moon — First African Secretary-General — South Korea
accepted.x: Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru was the first Latin American Secretary-General. Boutros-Ghali was the first African/Arab, Kofi Annan was from Ghana, and Ban Ki-moon was from South Korea.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure person-region pair and check both the title and country.
accepted.sec: Secretaries-General - order, FIRST by region, present SG

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Trygve Lie — Norway — 1946–1952
2. Dag Hammarskjold — Sweden — 1953–1961
3. Kurt Waldheim — Austria — 1972–1981
4. Antonio Guterres — Portugal — 2017 onwards
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the respective countries and tenure periods.
accepted.tq: Verify each country-tenure pair independently before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Secretaries-General - order, FIRST by region, present SG

accepted.s: The Secretary-General of the United Nations is described in the Charter framework as the
accepted.x: The Secretary-General is the Chief Administrative Officer of the United Nations and may bring threats to peace to the attention of the Security Council.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the administrative role from judicial, electoral and military functions.
accepted.sec: Secretaries-General - order, FIRST by region, present SG

accepted.s: Which principal organ of the United Nations has 54 members serving three-year terms and coordinates economic, social and Sustainable Development Goal-related work?
accepted.x: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) has 54 members with three-year terms and coordinates economic, social and SDG-related activities.
accepted.tq: Combine composition, tenure and mandate to identify the organ.
accepted.sec: Principal organs and subsidiary bodies - composition and mandate

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the principal organs of the United Nations:
1. The General Assembly consists of all 193 members, with one vote each.
2. The Security Council has 15 members and is the only UN body whose decisions bind members.
3. The Secretariat is headed by the Secretary-General.
4. The Trusteeship Council has remained active continuously since 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Trusteeship Council has been inactive since 1994, following the attainment of self-government by Palau.
accepted.tq: Look for the time-word reversal in the statement about the Trusteeship Council.
accepted.sec: Principal organs and subsidiary bodies - composition and mandate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: International Court of Justice — Principal judicial organ — The Hague
accepted.x: ECOSOC has 54 members serving three-year terms, not 15 members serving two-year terms. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the composition and tenure mismatch in an otherwise familiar institutional list.
accepted.sec: Principal organs and subsidiary bodies - composition and mandate

accepted.s: Which commission reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration before being replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013?
o: Commission on the Status of Women
accepted.x: The Commission on Sustainable Development reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration and was replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013.
accepted.tq: Link a body with both its mandate and institutional successor.
accepted.sec: Principal organs and subsidiary bodies - composition and mandate

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the composition and election of the United Nations Security Council is correct?
o: The 10 non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly by a two-thirds secret ballot for two years and cannot be immediately re-elected.
The five permanent members are elected every two years by secret ballot.
All 15 members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.
The 10 non-permanent members are appointed by ECOSOC for three-year terms.
accepted.x: The Security Council has five permanent and ten non-permanent members. The ten non-permanent members are elected by a two-thirds secret ballot of the General Assembly for two years and are not eligible for immediate re-election.
accepted.tq: Check the authority, majority, ballot method and tenure together.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s: Under Article 27, the veto in the United Nations Security Council is held by
o: the General Assembly as a whole
the Secretary-General and the P5 jointly
accepted.x: The five permanent members—China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States—possess the veto under Article 27.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority that holds the power rather than the body where the vote occurs.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s: Which one of the following lists contains all the countries elected to the Security Council for the 2027–28 term?
o: Austria, India, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe
Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Japan, Trinidad and Tobago, Ghana
Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe
accepted.x: The countries elected for the 2027–28 term are Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago and Zimbabwe.
accepted.tq: Test complete list recall while using nearby states as membership traps.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s: How many times had India served as an elected non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council through the 2021–22 term?
accepted.tq: Count the complete sequence of terms rather than the number of years served.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s: India launched its candidature for the 2028–29 term of the United Nations Security Council on 13 July 2026. Its rival candidate was
accepted.x: India's bid was launched by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in New York, while Tajikistan, backed by the OIC, was the rival candidate.
accepted.tq: Match the candidature with the rival and supporting organisation.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s: In the April 2024 vote on full UN membership for Palestine, which combination correctly describes the votes against or abstentions that meant the proposal did not receive unanimous support?
o: Russia vetoed; the United Kingdom and India abstained.
China vetoed; India and France abstained.
The United States vetoed; France and Germany abstained.
The United States vetoed; the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained.
accepted.x: The United States used its veto, while the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained; three members therefore did not vote in favour.
accepted.tq: Track the different actions—veto and abstention—rather than treating all as negative votes.
accepted.sec: UNSC - members, term and election, veto, India's terms, recent votes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations General Assembly:
1. Every member has one vote.
2. Important questions require a two-thirds majority.
3. The Holy See and Palestine have non-member observer-state status.
4. The Credentials Committee has nine members appointed for each session.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the General Assembly follows one-member-one-vote, important questions require a two-thirds majority, the Holy See and Palestine are observer states, and the Credentials Committee has nine members appointed each session.
accepted.tq: Combine voting, observer status and committee composition in a single institutional profile.
accepted.sec: UNGA - voting, observers, Credentials Committee, emergency sessions, Uniting for Peace, Presidents

accepted.s: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Uniting for Peace Resolution as Resolution 377 in
accepted.x: Resolution 377, known as Uniting for Peace, was adopted in 1950. It permits the General Assembly to act when a veto prevents the Security Council from acting.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of adoption from the later crisis in which the resolution was first used.
accepted.sec: UNGA - voting, observers, Credentials Committee, emergency sessions, Uniting for Peace, Presidents

accepted.s: The Uniting for Peace Resolution was first used in the 1956
accepted.x: Resolution 377 was first used during the 1956 Suez Crisis to facilitate the sending of peacekeepers.
accepted.tq: Separate the name of the resolution from the historical situation in which it was first applied.
accepted.sec: UNGA - voting, observers, Credentials Committee, emergency sessions, Uniting for Peace, Presidents

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the President of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly:
1. Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh was elected for 2026–27.
2. He defeated the candidate from Cyprus.
3. The presidency rotates among five regional groups.
4. The President of the General Assembly has a vote in every General Assembly matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The President of the General Assembly does not vote, making statement 4 false.
accepted.tq: Identify the single role-related false statement among correct election details.
accepted.sec: UNGA - voting, observers, Credentials Committee, emergency sessions, Uniting for Peace, Presidents

accepted.s: In May 2026, India abstained on a United Nations General Assembly climate resolution adopted with which voting result?
accepted.x: India abstained on the climate resolution, which recorded 141 votes in favour, 8 against and 28 abstentions. The resolution cited the ICJ's July 2025 climate advisory opinion.
accepted.tq: Read the three-part voting figures in the correct order: in favour, against and abstentions.
accepted.sec: UNGA - voting, observers, Credentials Committee, emergency sessions, Uniting for Peace, Presidents
